source.title: Probing Large Language Model Hidden States for Adverse Drug Reaction Knowledge
source.authors: J. Berkowitz; D. Weissenbacher; A. Srinivasan; N. Friedrich; J. M. Acitores Cortina; S. Kivelson; G. G. Hernandez; N. Tatonetti

record.tranche_reason: The study probes pretrained LLM activations with SAE-derived features and reports whether those features retain predictive information. It does not reproduce the toy-model superposition experiment or measure its feature geometry.
record.gate_note: The study also reports text-generation classification results, but those do not measure the representation claims. Feature descriptions and the speculative interpretation of an individual feature are not separate results bearing on the listed versions.
record.test_reason: The study uses pretrained Gemma Scope SAEs as a feature extractor for ADR classification. It reports only its own pipeline's AUCs and compares them with raw-activation MLPs and prompting. None of its results measure feature overlap, neuron spread, capacity, SAE stability, completeness, canonicality or dimensionality. The 46.6% annotation measures topical relevance of L1-selected features, not whether SAE features are the model's units.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that SAE features from Gemma2-9b-it retain ADR-relevant information: linear probes match raw-activation MLPs and beat prompting. They note only partial monosemanticity and suggest larger SAEs might split features better.
record.recipe_differences: Uses pretrained Gemma Scope SAEs on a real LLM and evaluates downstream ADR classification; it does not implement toy networks, vary feature sparsity or importance, or measure superposition geometry.
record.method_sensitivity: The study compares SAE results across layers 9, 20, and 31; it reports pairwise AUC-distribution p-values and says the ranges overlap substantially.

fits_no_version.finding: Only 46.6% of L1-selected SAE features were judged 'somewhat science related', e.g. a footwear/ankle feature used for kidney injury.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE features selected by a downstream probe often lack obvious semantic relevance to the task.

record.peer_reviewed: medRxiv preprint; not certified by peer review
record.problems: Evidence is limited to one instruction-tuned model and one ADR benchmark. The paper gives no outcome-specific numeric comparisons against raw-activation classifiers and no direct ground-truth test of feature recovery. The monosemanticity assessment is described only as a brief manual annotation.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 3 includes comparisons of AUCs across methods and layers, but the supplied text gives no numerical values for those plotted comparisons. No separate figure-only rows were extracted.

untested.parts: All parts: no toy models, sparsity sweep or geometry.
All parts: no capacity or importance analysis.
Neuron-level spread of features and recovery of sparse features against ground truth. Only downstream probe AUC is reported.
Completeness, stability across runs or sizes, and canonicality. The SAE is used off the shelf.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests'/T2 classification and its V4/V5 labels are reversed here. This is an applied pharmacovigilance paper using SAEs as a tool. It cites Toy Models only to motivate SAEs. The prompting comparison (Results 3.2) is likewise a method comparison and bears on no version.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, feature overlap and geometry, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether polysemanticity results from capacity competition or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Whether polysemanticity arises for reasons other than capacity pressure.

The study tests SAE-derived feature usefulness for ADR classification in one model; it does not measure how many neurons encode each feature, directly establish feature recovery against ground truth, or test other models or domains.
It reports a manual annotation and partial monosemanticity, but does not test feature stability across contexts or runs, completeness, or canonicality.
Whether represented features are one-dimensional directions or multidimensional.

rows.subject: Gemma2-9b-it
rows.operation_detail: Transform layer 9 residual-stream activations with a pretrained Gemma Scope SAE, max-pool token features, and fit L1-regularized logistic regression.
rows.note: The SAE representation was used to classify drug-outcome pairs in the reference set.
rows.check: This is the study's own method's downstream AUC (acute kidney injury). Good probe accuracy on SAE features is not evidence about sparse feature recovery or neuron spread (V4).

relation.reason: Uses SAE representations as a tool without measuring superposition, feature recovery, dictionary completeness, stability, canonicality, or feature dimensionality.

tranche.reason: Uses pretrained Gemma Scope SAEs for downstream ADR classification; its performance and task-relevance measurements do not test V1–V6.

source_check.notes: The 46.6% annotation measures science relevance, not monosemanticity; comparable probe performance does not establish dictionary completeness. The prompting comparison reports acute liver injury p = 0.789, despite describing differences as significant for every ADR.
